findings: OQ-67 (a): the printed def:causally_open_spacetime_open (ETT.tex:694–697, J⁺ only) is strictly weaker than DEC-8's two-sided reading AMONG ABSOLUTELY MINIMAL causalities: the half-lit line on ℝ is absolutely minimal on every open set for every cover (so an ETT spacetime under the gluing reading of defi:causalite, ETT.tex:237–251, as well as the library's), causally arc-connected, globally hyperbolic, push-up, causally open in the future, and J⁻_M((1, 2)) = [0, 2) is not open (Causal.halfLightLine_separates_causallyOpen, not_causallyOpen_of_causallyOpenFuture_of_absolutelyMinimalOn_bare). So OQ-67 (b) no longer bears on this separation: it holds in either reading, pending OQ-18 or not. Confirming DEC-8's ± changes the notion; keeping the printed form keeps a strictly larger class.

The printed notion is not invariant under time reversal even for absolutely minimal causalities (not_dual_causallyOpenFuture_of_absolutelyMinimal_bare): with J⁺ only, 'causally open' depends on the time orientation, which the paper's past-from-future arguments (e.g. the proof of prop:tarentin_topological_spacetime_causality, ETT.tex:745–746, using J⁻ of an open set) silently assume it does not.

Scope of the finding: the half-lit line is NOT tarentin, so it does not show that the ± matters among tarentin spacetimes, the setting of prop:tarentin_topological_spacetime_causality (ETT.tex:713), the one statement whose proof needs J⁻. That stays open (see questions).
questions: Does the gap survive tarentin? Whether an absolutely minimal (or causally arc-connected) TARENTIN causality can be causally open in the future and not in the past is not settled here. If it cannot, the printed J⁺ form would suffice for prop:tarentin_topological_spacetime_causality and the ± of DEC-8 could be read as a convenience there; if it can, DEC-8 is needed for that proposition as printed. No reading taken; the half-lit line says nothing either way.

Reading of 'either reading of defi:causalite' taken here: the gluing reading is absolute minimality on every open set for every open cover of it (Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimalOn W for all W), as OQ-18 phrases it ('≤ generated by covers, i.e. absolute minimality'); the half-lit line satisfies both this and the library's AbsolutelyMinimal (covers of M), so the separation does not depend on which of the two is meant.
